expectations.text: Diagnoses that $var.<childJobId>.job_details may not resolve inside query.obj on some platform versions
expectations.evidence: No mention anywhere in the transcript or in either output file of $var.<childJobId>.job_details failing to resolve inside a query task's obj field on any platform version. The transcript's diagnosis section (lines 44-105) covers three causes: (1) misreading the query:'loop' result shape and needing '[**].taskStatus' wildcard projection, (2) the child workflow not setting taskStatus on every terminal branch, and (3) parallel-loop result ordering vs childJobLoopIndex. None of these is a resolution failure of $var.<childJobId>.job_details itself. Both output JSON files (fix-parent-loop-taskStatus-extraction.json lines 46 and 74) use 'obj': '$var.a1a1.job_details' directly and treat it as fully reliable, with no caveat about platform-version-dependent resolution failure. I also checked the underlying skill file consulted for this run (/private/tmp/eval-old-skill/builder-agent/SKILL.md) and grepped for 'does not resolve', 'may not resolve', and 'platform version' — the only documented $var non-resolution gotchas in that skill are for nested forEach bodies (line 1487/2198), stringConcat/value fields (lines 1503, 2162), none of which is the childJob job_details-in-query.obj case this expectation asks about. The skill itself does not contain this gotcha, so the executor had no way to surface it.

claims.claim: The delivered child-workflow fix (fix-child-workflow-taskstatus-coverage.json) is a correct, importable try-catch pattern with every terminal path setting taskStatus
claims.evidence: The file uses task id 'err1' for one of its newVariable tasks (line 106 of fix-child-workflow-taskstatus-coverage.json). The project's own AGENTS.md rule 9 explicitly states task IDs must be hex-only ([0-9a-f]{1,4}) and calls out 'err1' by name as an example of a non-hex ID that (a) causes $var references to silently fail at runtime and (b) causes project import to fail with a schema validation error. The delivered 'fix' file reintroduces exactly the invalid ID pattern the platform rules warn against, undermining the claim that it is a clean, ready-to-import corrected pattern.

suggestions.assertion: Does not discourage the direct $var.<childJobId>.job_details form as the default first attempt
suggestions.reason: This assertion passes almost by default whenever the executor doesn't know about the platform-version resolution gotcha at all (as here) — it can't meaningfully distinguish 'correctly kept the direct form as primary while also covering the fallback' from 'never learned about the fallback in the first place and so trivially never discouraged the default.' Consider rephrasing to require evidence that the direct form is *retained as primary* specifically alongside a documented awareness of the platform-version caveat, so a response that is simply ignorant of the whole issue doesn't pass by coincidence.

The delivered fix-child-workflow-taskstatus-coverage.json uses the non-hex task id 'err1', which AGENTS.md rule 9 in this very repo explicitly lists as a known-bad example (causes $var resolution failures and project-import schema errors). No expectation in this eval set checks task-ID validity, so a real, concrete defect in the produced artifact went completely uncaught. Consider adding an assertion that all task IDs in delivered workflow JSON match the hex-only pattern the platform requires.

eval_feedback.overall: This run's expectations are almost entirely about a specific, narrow platform gotcha (childJobId.job_details not resolving inside query.obj on some versions, and the merge+taskRef workaround) that is not documented anywhere in the old_skill's SKILL.md consulted for this run. The executor produced a well-grounded, internally-consistent diagnosis and fix for three other real causes of intermittent null taskStatus, and verifiably grounded its claims in real asset files rather than fabricating schema — but it had no way to surface a gotcha the skill doesn't teach. 3 of 4 expectations fail cleanly and for the right reason (this appears to be exactly the gap the skill update under test is meant to close). The 4th expectation passed but only trivially, since 'not discouraging' something never mentioned is a low bar; and the eval missed catching a real, verifiable defect (the invalid 'err1' task ID) in the delivered output.
